name: conscroll
description: A WRITE THAT SCROLLS PAINTS EVERY ROW IT SCROLLED IN, asserted against the PIXELS.  While a console write is open a full-screen scroll is counted instead of moved, and the pixels move once when the write ends, by every row it scrolled (console_scroll.s _Con_FlushPending).  `cat' of 150 lines makes each write(2) scroll many rows at once, so the end-of-write flush is what paints the bottom of the screen.  conpaint_check.py compares the SHR framebuffer with the CharBuf cell by cell after the command; a flush that moves the pixels but does not render the exposed rows fails it (measured).  The input comes from a man page with head(1) so no fixture is needed; the MARKDONE sentinel ends the run when the output does, because the shell's own prompts scroll out of the CharBuf.
